newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says World Bank aid to help industry.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says World Bank aid to help industry.

text.p: Thailand's Board of Investment (BOI) said on Monday up to $1.5 billion in aid from the World Bank will be used to help Thailand restructure its export-related industries.
A senior BOI official said the details of the loans would be discussed next month when World Bank delegates visit Thailand.
The World Bank said in a statement received on Sunday that it pledged the money at a meeting in Tokyo last week.
"At the Tokyo meeting, the World Bank pledged $1.5 billion of support focused on improving Thailand's competitiveness and prompting structural reforms in the economy," the statement said.

"Discussions held with Thai officials have resulted in the identification of areas of concentration, which includes the financial and banking sector, export promotion, labour productivity and social safety nets," it added.
The BOI official said the board was singling out potential industries to restructure under the scheme in order to boost competitiveness.
Thailand exports contracted 0.2 percent in 1996 against growth of more than 25 percent in 1995. Analysts attributed the plunge in export growth to both cyclical and structural problems.
